description: Maps every onboarding field to TRAIN programming logic. This is the bridge between client intake data and AI program generation.
author: Kim Valles Coaching, LLC

name.use: Personalize all communication. Always address client by first name.

programming_notes.under_25: Higher recovery capacity. Can handle higher frequency and volume.
programming_notes.40_to_50: Begin factoring in recovery time. Slightly more deload emphasis. Joint-friendly movement selection.
programming_notes.50_plus: Prioritize mobility, joint integrity, and recovery. Reduce high-impact loading. Emphasize longevity over intensity.

programming_notes.F: Account for hormonal cycle impact on energy and recovery where relevant. Females often respond well to higher rep ranges for hypertrophy.

height_weight.use: Body composition context. Do not prescribe calorie targets. Use weight for relative load suggestions (e.g. bodyweight-based benchmarks).

fat_loss.priority: Preserve lean muscle while creating caloric deficit through training. Higher rep ranges (12–20). Shorter rest (45–75s). Include cardio or conditioning. Emphasize compound movements for caloric demand.

muscle_gain.priority: Progressive overload is king. Rep ranges 6–12 for hypertrophy. Longer rest (90–180s). Volume over intensity in early phases.
muscle_gain.weekly_volume: Higher — track total sets per muscle group

body_recomp.priority: Simultaneously reduce fat and build muscle. Requires precise training balance — enough volume for hypertrophy, enough density for fat loss. Kim's signature coaching outcome.
body_recomp.split_bias: Upper/lower 4x or Full body 3x for beginners
body_recomp.rep_ranges: 8–12 primary compound, 12–15 accessory — the sweet spot between hypertrophy and fat loss stimulus
body_recomp.rest: 60–90s — longer than fat loss, shorter than pure hypertrophy
body_recomp.cardio: 2–3 sessions — moderate intensity, not aggressive. Cardio supports recomp but does not dominate.
body_recomp.nutrition_flag: Note protein_awareness in program header — recomp requires adequate protein. If not_tracking, include a gentle protein note in program intro.
body_recomp.experience_note: Best results for intermediate+. Beginners will naturally recomp on any program — manage expectations gently.
body_recomp.key_distinction: Fat loss clients lose weight. Muscle gain clients add size. Recomp clients may see minimal scale change but dramatic body composition shift — prepare client for this with clear framing.

performance.priority: Power, speed, athleticism. Mix of strength (3–5 reps) and conditioning. Compound and explosive movements priority.

general_health.priority: Consistency and enjoyment over optimization. Balanced movement. Mobility included every session. Rep ranges 10–15.

goal_detail.use: Specific outcome stated by client (e.g. 'lose 15 lbs', 'fit into size 8', 'deadlift 200 lbs'). Reference this when setting 8-week milestones and framing progress.

beginner.exercise_complexity: Foundational movements only. Master the pattern before adding load. Avoid advanced variations.
beginner.sets_reps: 2–3 sets, 10–15 reps. Light to moderate load.
beginner.progression: Frequency and form first. Add reps before weight.
beginner.coaching_cues: Verbose — explain every movement. No assumed knowledge.

intermediate.exercise_complexity: Full exercise library available. Can introduce tempo and supersets.
intermediate.sets_reps: 3–4 sets, 8–12 reps. Moderate load with RPE 7–8.
intermediate.progression: Add weight every 1–2 weeks when RIR allows.

advanced.exercise_complexity: All variations available. Periodization, undulating reps, advanced techniques.
advanced.sets_reps: 4–5 sets, 4–12 reps depending on phase. High RPE (8–9).

recent_training.use: Understand actual movement base. A 'beginner' who has been doing yoga for 2 years has better body awareness and mobility than a true sedentary beginner. Adjust accordingly.

programming_notes.rarely: Treat as beginner regardless of stated experience. Low volume start. Habit-building priority.
programming_notes.1-2x: Conservative volume. Build to target frequency over 2–3 weeks.
programming_notes.3-4x: Can match or slightly exceed current volume.
programming_notes.5x+: High capacity. Can handle full target volume from week 1.

split_mapping.2: Full body both days. Focus on compound movements only.
split_mapping.4: Upper/Lower split. Or Full body x2 + accessory x2.
split_mapping.5: PPL + 2 full body OR Upper/Lower + extra session.
split_mapping.7: PPL x2 + active recovery. Flag recovery risk.

exercise_count_guide.60_to_90_min: 8–10 exercises. Full warm-up, mobility, finisher possible.
exercise_count_guide.90_plus_min: Full program. Warm-up, main block, accessory, finisher, cooldown.

values.full_gym: All exercises available. Barbell, cables, machines, dumbbells.
values.home_gym: Dumbbell-based. Resistance bands. Bodyweight. No barbell unless stated.
values.minimal: Bodyweight + bands only. Reference substitution map for all exercises.
values.mixed: Build primary program for minimal. Note full-gym upgrade options per exercise.

injuries.use: Cross-reference with injury_navigation.json. Flag contraindicated movements. Provide safe substitutions. Never ignore this field.
injuries.critical_note: If injury field is non-empty, always acknowledge in program notes and modify accordingly.

programming_impact.poor: Reduce volume by 15–20%. Prioritize recovery. Flag deload more frequently.
programming_impact.great: Can push volume and intensity to upper ranges.

programming_impact.high: Reduce volume 10–15%. Emphasize movement quality over load. Include breathing/cooldown.
programming_impact.very_high: Conservative volume. Prioritize nervous system recovery. Shorter sessions. More full-body, less split-intensive.

exercise_modifications.tight_hips: Avoid deep squat variations until addressed. Substitute goblet squat with heel elevation. Add hip flexor work to warm-up.
exercise_modifications.limited_shoulder: Avoid overhead pressing initially. Substitute dumbbell press angles. No barbell back squat — use safety bar or goblet. Add shoulder mobility to warm-up.
exercise_modifications.ankle_restriction: Elevate heels for squat patterns. Avoid deep lunge variations. Add ankle mobility drills.
exercise_modifications.thoracic_stiffness: Add thoracic extension to warm-up. Avoid loaded rotation under fatigue. Cue bracing on all pressing.
exercise_modifications.hamstring_tightness: Limit Romanian deadlift range initially. Add hamstring stretching post-session. Cue soft knee on all hinge patterns.
exercise_modifications.wrist_discomfort: Substitute barbell with dumbbell or neutral grip. Avoid front rack positions. Add wrist warm-up.

coaching_approach.low: Include detailed mind-muscle cues in every exercise. Recommend lighter load to feel the muscle. Reference mind_muscle_connection.json for cue language.
coaching_approach.moderate: Standard cues. Reinforce connection on isolation work.
coaching_approach.high: Minimal cueing needed. Can introduce advanced techniques (pause reps, tempos, blood flow restriction).

meal_frequency.use: Context for energy availability. Not for prescribing diet. Flag very low meal frequency as potential recovery risk if training volume is high.
meal_frequency.note: 1–2 meals with 5x/week training = flag for energy management conversation.

coaching_notes.not_tracking: Gently introduce protein importance in program notes. Keep it simple — not prescriptive.
coaching_notes.somewhat: Affirm the habit. Offer general guidance only.
coaching_notes.intentional: No additional nutrition notes needed in program.

nutrition_challenge.use: Context for coaching language. Reference Kim's system prompt for how to address emotional eating, meal skipping, etc. Never shame or prescribe.

coaching_language.performance_data: Lead progress updates with metrics — reps added, weight increased, time improved. Frame workouts in terms of performance outcomes.
coaching_language.feeling_energy: Lead with identity and feeling language. 'How did that feel?' over 'what did you lift?' Reference Kim's affirmation language.
coaching_language.both: Balance metrics with feeling check-ins. Alternate framing week to week.

coaching_response.reminder_why: When client is struggling — reconnect to vision and identity statement. Pull directly from their intake answers.
coaching_response.simplify: When struggling — strip program down. One exercise. One set. Just show up.
coaching_response.accountability: When struggling — direct check-in. Name the pattern. Hold the standard with warmth.
coaching_response.space: When struggling — acknowledge and step back. No pressure. Let them come back.

fitness_evolution.use: Understand client's relationship with fitness over time. Informs pacing, expectations, and how to frame progress. Reference when motivating or addressing setbacks.

best_results.use: What has worked before. Mirror successful elements in current program structure where possible. Reference when client loses motivation.

consistency_blockers.use: Anticipate and proactively address in program design. If 'time' is a blocker — keep sessions tight. If 'boredom' — vary exercise selection. If 'injury' — build injury prevention in.

current_physical_state.use: Snapshot of where client is right now physically. Cross-reference with sleep, stress, and mobility. Informs starting volume and intensity.

identity_statement.use: Pull this verbatim when client is struggling or needs a reset. This is their own words about who they are when they show up — the most powerful coaching tool in the profile.

vision.use: The 'why' behind everything. Reference at program start, at plateau moments, and at milestone completions. Frame all progress in terms of this vision.

program_generation_instructions.step_1_read_profile: Load all fields above. Note any flags (injuries, very high stress, poor sleep, minimal equipment).
program_generation_instructions.step_2_assess_starting_point: Cross-reference experience + recent_frequency + current_physical_state to determine true starting volume and intensity.
program_generation_instructions.step_3_select_split: Use days_per_week + goal + split_mapping to choose training split.
program_generation_instructions.step_4_build_sessions: Use session_length + equipment + exercise libraries + movement_categories.json to build each day.
program_generation_instructions.step_5_apply_variables: Apply sets, reps, tempo, rest from programming_variables.json filtered by goal + experience.
program_generation_instructions.step_6_injury_check: Run all exercises against injury_navigation.json. Substitute any flagged movements.
program_generation_instructions.step_7_apply_voice: Use motivation_style + struggle_style + system_prompt.md to write program notes in TRAIN's voice.
program_generation_instructions.step_8_set_progression: Define week-over-week progression using periodization.json. Set deload on week 4 or 5.
